newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French PIBOR interest rate futures finished Matif trading firmer, lifted by the Bank of France's small interest rate cut on Thursday afternoon.
Bond futures finished pit-trading firmer too, tracking Bunds and other European debt markets higher after the U.S. market's rise overnight. A stronger U.S. opening helped support bonds.
The Bank of France trimmed a further five basis points off the intervention rate, to 3.10 from 3.15 percent, which came as a surprise to some in pure timing terms.
One trader said the bond future's finish could open the way for an advance that could test the contract high of 131.16.

But he said this would require a T-Bond move above 110.25 and progress by the Bund beyond 101.40, while in the shorter term, the market was likely to remain cautious ahead of U.S. fourth quarter GDP figures at 1330 GMT on Friday.
In interest rate futures, PIBOR rose across several contracts, with March PIBOR settling five basis points higher, having stood three basis points up ahead of the rate cut news.
"Some people believed in it (a rate cut), but it hadn't really been written into the level," said one trader.

Fourth quarter U.S. GDP is expected to advance 3.9 percent according to an average of forecasts compiled by Reuters and the Chigaco Purchasing Managers index, due at 1500 GMT is seen coming in at 57.4 for January.

Some analysts say too strong a GDP figure could be read by the market as a sign the Federal Reserve, whose FOMC committee meets on February 4-5, is taking too lax a stand on inflation, while conversely, a lowish number would prolong the speculation about a possible rate rise.
The Fed funds rate stands at 5.25 percent and has not moved since a cut in 1996.
The view among economists is that more French cuts are on the way and PIBOR was helped after today's small cut, with a rise across several contracts out along the curve.
While the timing of the French cut surprised, the general view is that the Bank of France is pushing the intervention rate towards the German repo rate of 3.0 percent.

The cut prompted some to suggest the two new members of the monetary policy council, Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard, may be tilting the the balance to more rapid action after the departure of two men seen as defenders of a cautious policy.

"I believe (Bank governor Jean-Claude) Trichet would have wanted to wait for the FOMC decision next week," Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley in Paris said. "But the doves wanted to send a strong message, so this might be a compromise."
"It seems the doves are decisive, it's not just a dream -- since the two new member joined. They'll cut further in the coming months," said ABN Amro's Philippe Brossard.
In the cash market, yields on the 6.50 percent OAT due 2006 eased to 5.62 from 5.63, with the spread of the equivalent Bund contracting marginally to minus 17 from minus 18.
